record.paper_title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can declarative mapping languages for large knowledge bases, such as R2R, be used to express knowledge-base mapping rules in a form that can be optimized and then compiled into SPARQL or another execution language?

evidence.quote: An interesting open question is to study the use of declarative languages like R2R that can perhaps be optimized and then “compiled” into SPARQL or other execution languages.

artifact.category_tag: declarative mapping languages for knowledge bases
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let a knowledge base be a set of RDF triples over an infinite set of IRIs and literals, and let a mapping rule between two such knowledge bases be a function that, given a source pattern (a conjunctive query over the source RDF graph), produces a target pattern (a set of RDF triples possibly containing variables bound by the source pattern). Consider a declarative mapping language L (for instance, one in the style of R2R) whose expressions denote finite sets of such mapping rules, equipped with a formal semantics that, given a source RDF graph, yields a target RDF graph.

Formulate and answer the following:

(1) Define a declarative mapping language L expressive enough to capture a useful class of knowledge-base-to-knowledge-base mapping rules, and give it a precise denotational semantics in terms of RDF graphs.

(2) Define a notion of equivalence between expressions of L (two expressions are equivalent if they yield identical target graphs for every source graph) and a notion of optimization (a rewriting relation preserving this equivalence, intended to reduce some cost measure such as the size of intermediate results or query evaluation time).

(3) Provide a compilation function C from L into SPARQL (or another standard execution language) such that for every expression e of L and every source RDF graph G, evaluating C(e) on G returns the same target graph as the semantics of e on G.

(4) Prove the correctness of the compilation and demonstrate that nontrivial optimizations at the level of L can be performed before compilation in a way that yields more efficient SPARQL queries than naive compilation followed by SPARQL-level optimization.

Determine whether such a language, semantics, optimization framework, and compilation can be realized, and characterize the class of mapping rules for which this is possible.
artifact.status_search_result: No definitive resolution was found. Work on declarative RDF mapping languages (R2RML, SPARQL-Generate, RML, ShExML) and their compilation/optimization into SPARQL exists, but a complete, formally verified optimization-then-compilation framework matching the question as posed does not appear to have been established as a single solved problem.

status_evidence.title: R2RML: RDB to RDF Mapping Language
status_evidence.snippet: W3C Recommendation defining a declarative mapping language from relational databases to RDF.
status_evidence.claim: Declarative RDF mapping languages exist and have standardized semantics, but the specific optimization-and-compile-to-SPARQL question remains an active research direction rather than a closed result.
